Starting from here: https://greaterthangames.com/comment/90731#comment-90731 the topic has become about reducing the next damage Mister Fixer takes and how would could interact with Driving Mantis.

Using the Video Game, I have run a few scenerios that would help determine how it currently would handle this situation. The following is the conclusion I have come to.

  1. If the damage is reduced to 0, Mister Fixer would not be able to redirect it and the damage reduction is expended.
  2. If the damage is reduced to 1 or 2 and Mister Fixer would not be able to redirect the base damage (it without any modifiers), then the damage reduction will be expended and Mister Fixer will redirect as normal.
  3. If the damage is reduced to 1 or 2 and Mister Fixer would have been able to redirect the base damage (it without any modifiers), then the damage reduction will be still be avaliable for the next attack and Mister Fixer will redirect as normal.

 

And I believe that is pretty much it.

Reduction is always a factor in the equation, whether or not it is a defining factor or not.  Prevention is always prevention, whether it had qualifications or not.

Undaunted doesn't prevent 1 point of damage, it prevents damage dealt to her when that damge would deal 1 damage.

When that qualification of being 1 damage is checked if it is 1 damage the whole rpocess is prevented, the dealer never dealt damage, that is what prevention is.

It works the same as any other prevention, it just only works when its qualifications are met.

 

The samge with redirection, if damage would be dealt to a target and that damage, qualifications or not, is redirected the damage is re-targetted, and no attack is made against the initial target.

 

You don't reduce damage on attacks that were never made.  When an attack is prevented or redirected that original potential attack didn't happen.

phantaskippy:

You don't reduce damage on attacks that were never made.  When an attack is prevented or redirected that original potential attack didn't happen.

If that were true, the redirection would never have been possible. That's precisely the point I'm trying to make. I'm taking issue with the fact that the game checks to see if the one-time reduction is expended if HP is reduced from its intended target, not whether or not it cushioned the blow, which it did. It feels like a giant loophole to benefit from the one-time modifier when it's convenient, but to remove its expendature when it's not.

Edit: Just to be clear, I have no problem with preserving a one-time modifier if there is no need to consume it. If Nightmist redirects 3 fire damage, and Haka chose to target Nightmist with shielding, then there is no need to worry about whether or not Shielding is consumed. However, Fixer NEEDS the damage to be reduced. So the reduction is applied but not consumed since it doesn't hit him during this instance and ANY instance after that, as long as the oncoming damage doesn't exceed 4. And if Haka discards even more cards, Fixer becomes a perfect shield with redirection, given his Mantis isn't destroyed, and that it is the first instance of damage each turn. That's more powerful than Flesh to Iron and Nightmist's pendant combined.

I may be a bit too adamant about this, but I feel for a fun and balanced gameplay experience, things like this should be addressed. That's what rulings and errata are for, right? And perhaps the majority of the problem lies with Fixer, perhaps we can forgive one-time modifiers.

Not to mention, the "would be dealt" on Mantis vs "dealt" text on Shielding makes for an interesting case on whether or not the interaction is even possible.
